result.title: Support-Guided Triadic Decoding for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Dialogue with LVLMs
result.summary: In multimodal multi-turn dialogue, dialogue history plays a dual role: reliable responses provide useful context for subsequent turns, whereas hallucinated responses can propagate errors across turns. Existing training-free methods globally adjust the effect of dialogue history on generation, making it difficult to suppress misleading information without weakening useful context. To address this trade-off, we introduce Support-Guided Triadic Decoding (SGTD), a training-free framework that selectively controls the influence of unreliable history and fuses complementary predictions during decoding. Specifically, Historical Answer Support Estimation measures the visual support of historical responses against type-matched alternatives and identifies low-support content that may mislead later generation. Support-Targeted Attention Intervention then weakens the influence of this content while preserving the surrounding dialogue, producing a support-refined prediction. Triadic Decoding combines this prediction with the full-history prediction and answer-free visual evidence, while the Support-Adaptive Plausibility Constraint filters implausible tokens using visual agreement and historical support. Experiments on MMHalSnowball and VisDiaHalBench across representative LVLMs show that SGTD consistently achieves the highest accuracy under hallucinated histories while preserving the benefits of factual context.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出免训练的 SGTD 解码框架，用于多模态多轮对话中的幻觉抑制：先估计历史回答相对于同类型候选的视觉支持度，据此通过注意力干预削弱低支持历史的影响，再将精炼预测、全历史预测与无答案视觉证据三路融合，并用视觉一致性与历史支持度约束候选词。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按视觉支持度筛选历史内容并在解码期融合多路证据的做法，与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、答案是否真正使用视觉信息以及错误传播的诊断问题直接相关，可供核查支持度估计能否作为潜在状态的质量信号。
